newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's AWB holds wheat pool prices steady.
newsitem.headline: Australia's AWB holds wheat pool prices steady.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said on Monday it had held its 1996/97 and 1997/98 pool price estimates unchanged.

The estimate for 1996/97 Australian Standard White (ASW) is unchanged at A$198 a tonne in the Number One pool and at A$185 a tonne in the Number Two pool. The Number One pool was closed two weeks ago and the Number Two pool opened.
The 1997/98 pool price for ASW is estimated in a steady range of A$180.00-A$190.00 a tonne.

The AWB on Monday also released first estimates in a breakdown of grades for the 1997/98 pool. Australian Prime Hard (APH) has been estimated at a A$25.00 premium to ASW, Australian Hard (AH) at a A$12.50 premium and Australian Premium White (APW) at a A$5.00 premium to ASW, the AWB said.

"There have been no significant developments in the wheat market over the last few weeks and prices have continued to be under pressure from the winter wheat harvest in the Northern Hemisphere," Ron Storey, general manager merchandising, said in a statement.
"Export demand is seasonally low, which has contributed to the ongoing weakness in the market," he said.

"As expected, the U.S. Department of Agriculture has confirmed an increase in (its) forecast of U.S. wheat production, at 66.2 million tonnes ... an increase of 3.5 million tonnes from (the) previous forecast," he said.
"This has maintained the market's focus on U.S. crop conditions and Southern Hemisphere growing conditions will be more of a concern as the season progresses," he said.
The next pool update will be issued on August 4.
